page.layout: One printed page, single column of text. Top: running head with page number at left. Then two short poems under "AD EANDEM." headings, an ornamental woodcut band, then the title block centred (GEORGII BUCHANANI SCOTI, DE SPHAERA LIB. I.) and the opening paragraph with a decorated initial, ending with the catchword "Dum" at the lower right.

main_text.head: AD EANDEM.
main_text.p:
Qvae melior meritis mihi fors Betona dedit te,
Hac cito sed meritis det precor aequa tuis.
main_text.head: AD EANDEM.
main_text.p:
Horret hyems, nec prata nitet, nec floribus horti,
Vnde queam dominae serta parare meae.
Quisque fuit cultu Musarum fertilis hortus
Ingenij, aetatis frigore stringit hyems.
Si tamen adspiret Zephyrus Betonidos aura,
Hic etiam invernas luxuriabit opes.
main_text.head: GEORGII BVCHANANI SCOTI,
DE SPHAERA LIB. I.
main_text.p: Qvam varia mundi partes, quo semina rerum (umbra Foedere conueniant discordia, lucis & Tempora quis motus regat, estum frigore mutet, Obscuret Solis vultum Lunaeque tenebris, Pandere fert animus. Tu qui fulgentia puro Lumine templa habitas oculis imperiua nostris, Rerum sancte parens audacibus annue coeptis: Dum late in populos ferimus tua facta, polique Immensum referamus opus: gens nescia veri Vt residem longaque animum caligine mersum Attollat coelo, & flammantia moenia mundi Dum

page.notes: The woodcut initial Q/V is decorated; the first word reads "Vàm" with the initial V. Several words in the body are faint or obscured by show-through and stains (e.g. "(umbra", "estum", "imperiua"); the readings are uncertain. The ornamental band between the poems and the title is a decorative woodcut, not text. A small page signature mark appears at the foot (a dot-like mark) and is not transcribed.
